Grayson County 64th in Kentucky for HUD-assisted units in 2025
S. O. Wilson
Grayson County placed 64th among 119 Kentucky counties in the 2025 Summary of All HUD Programs assisted-unit ranking, with 221 assisted units.
Assisted units increased by 6 from 215 in 2024.
HUD-assisted housing programs typically lower rent for eligible low-income households. HUD's Picture of Subsidized Households outlines three main categories of assistance: public housing, tenant-based assistance and privately owned, project-based assistance. Public housing is owned by local housing agencies, while tenant-based assistance, including housing vouchers, enables households to lease homes in the private market. Project-based assistance is tied to specific privately owned properties under HUD rental-assistance contracts.
Households receiving HUD rental assistance typically pay rent equal to 30% of their income after allowable deductions, with the federal government covering the remainder. Eligibility is based on HUD income limits that vary by location and household size, and applicants are usually placed on waiting lists until assistance becomes available.
